summary: Resolve pricing conflicts, check the Copilot/OpenRouter/Perplexity routes, and hunt hidden costs before totals

answers.question: Copilot Free's exact monthly AI-credit allowance
answers.answer: Not stated as a number anywhere on official GitHub pages. GitHub Free is described only as having "an allowance of GitHub AI Credits" / "Limited chat and agent usage," with no purchase option for more credits and no numeric figure published. The only hard numbers given for Free are 2,000 code completions/month (completions are billed separately from AI credits and are not credit-limited on paid plans). Checked 3 independent official pages (github.com/features/copilot/plans, docs.github.com Plans page, docs.github.com Usage-based billing for individuals) — all three omit the number.
answers.quote: Copilot Free and Copilot Student both have an allowance of AI credits and access to models through auto model selection only. Copilot Free includes 2000 code completions per month and Copilot Student includes unlimited code completions.

answers.question: Which models Copilot Free can use
answers.answer: Copilot Free (and Copilot Student) get models only via "auto model selection" — there is no manual model picker. GitHub does not publicly enumerate which underlying models the auto-selector draws from for the Free tier specifically; the per-plan model-availability table on docs.github.com only has columns for Pro/Pro+/Max/Business/Enterprise, not Free. The auto-selection page states auto model selection "chooses from supported models, subject to your policies and subscription type," implying a subscription-restricted subset, but the list is not published for Free.
answers.quote: Copilot Student and Copilot Free users have access to models through auto model selection only.

answers.question: Copilot Pro price and included AI credits
answers.answer: $10 USD/month (free for some verified students/teachers/OSS maintainers). Total 1,500 AI credits/month, split into 1,000 "base credits" (fixed, matches subscription price) + 500 "flex allotment" (variable, applied automatically after base is used). Confirmed identically on 3 independent official pages: github.com/features/copilot/plans, docs.github.com Plans page, and docs.github.com Usage-based billing for individuals.

answers.question: Do unused Copilot Pro AI credits carry over month to month?
answers.answer: No. Credits do not carry over; unused credits are forfeited and the allowance resets on the 1st of each calendar month at 00:00 UTC, regardless of your billing date.
answers.quote: Included AI credits do not carry over between months. Unused credits are forfeited, and your allowance resets to the full monthly amount at 00:00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month. This reset date is fixed and does not change based on your subscription billing date.

answers.question: Per-model AI-credit rates: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna (OpenAI)
answers.answer: All prices per 1M tokens; convert to AI credits by multiplying dollars by 100 (1 credit = $0.01). GPT-6 Astra (Powerful): Default tier (≤272K input tokens): input $10.00 (1,000 credits), cached input $1.00 (100 credits), cache write $12.50 (1,250 credits), output $50.00 (5,000 credits). Long-context tier (>272K): input $20.00, cached $2.00, cache write $25.00, output $75.00. GPT-5.6 Sol (Powerful): Default (≤272K): input $4.00, cached $0.40, cache write $5.00, output $20.00. Long-context (>272K): input $8.00, cached $0.80, cache write $10.00, output $30.00. GPT-5.6 Luna (Lightweight): Default (≤200K, note different threshold than Sol/Astra): input $0.20, cached $0.02, cache write $0.25, output $1.20. Long-context (>200K): input $0.40, cached $0.04, cache write $0.50, output $1.80.
answers.quote: GPT-6 Astra | GA | Powerful | Default | ≤ 272K | $10.00 | $1.00 | $12.50 | $50.00

answers.question: Per-model AI-credit rates: Gemini models available in Copilot
answers.answer: All per 1M tokens (no cache-write line for Gemini; multiply $ by 100 for AI credits). Gemini 3.5 Flash (Lightweight): input $1.50, cached input $0.15, output $9.00 — standard pricing, no promo. Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.7 Flash, 3.8 Flash (Versatile): input $0.75, cached $0.075, output $3.75 each, but this is explicitly PROMOTIONAL pricing valid only through December 31, 2026 (footnote 1 on all three) — flag that the rate changes after that date and the new rate is not stated.
answers.quote: Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.7 Flash, and Gemini 3.8 Flash are available at the promotional pricing of $0.75 per 1M input tokens, $0.075 per 1M cached input tokens, and $3.75 per 1M output tokens through December 31, 2026.

answers.answer: All per 1M tokens (Anthropic models all include a cache-write cost). Claude Haiku 4.5: input $1.00, cached $0.10, cache write $1.25, output $5.00. Claude Sonnet 4: $3.00 / $0.30 / $3.75 / $15.00. Claude Sonnet 4.6: same as Sonnet 4 — $3.00 / $0.30 / $3.75 / $15.00. Claude Sonnet 5: $2.00 / $0.20 / $2.50 / $10.00. Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode, preview): $10.00 / $1.00 / $12.50 / $50.00. Claude Fable 5: $10.00 / $1.00 / $12.50 / $50.00. Claude Fable 5.1: $10.00 / $0.25 / $12.50 / $50.00. Note: Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 also carry a separate data-retention/ZDR caveat (Anthropic retains prompts/outputs by default for safety classifiers unless enterprise-approved ZDR) — not a pricing term but relevant if these are ever used for the benchmark.

answers.question: Can Copilot CLI run one prompt non-interactively, and with what flags/output format?
answers.answer: Yes. `copilot -p "PROMPT"` (or piping to `copilot`) runs a single prompt and exits without an interactive session. Key flags for scripting: `-s` suppresses session metadata/decoration for clean text output; `--no-ask-user` stops it pausing for clarification; `--model=MODEL` pins a model; `--allow-tool=...` / `--allow-all` control tool permissions. Output format is controlled by `--output-format=FORMAT`: `text` (default) or `json`, where json mode emits JSONL (one JSON object per line) for easy script parsing.
answers.quote: --output-format=FORMAT | Set the output format: text (the default) or json. With json, the CLI emits JSONL (one JSON object per line), which is convenient for parsing the agent's output in scripts.

answers.question: Can Copilot CLI search the web, and how is that billed?
answers.answer: Yes, but general web search is only documented as part of the `/research` slash command (a specialized built-in research agent) and, more narrowly, a `url` tool that fetches specific allowed URLs/domains under `--allow-url`/`--allow-tool=url(...)` — there is no separate generic 'websearch' tool documented outside `/research`. On billing: no page checked (models-and-pricing, usage-based billing for individuals/orgs, CLI docs) lists a separate charge for web search or tool calls. Under the current AI-credits system, billing is purely per-token by model (input/cached/cache-write/output), so web-search/tool-call activity is billed only insofar as it adds tokens to the conversation — there is no discrete 'per search' fee documented. (Note: this confirms current AI-credit billing does NOT itemize tool calls; the legacy request-based billing model explicitly excluded autonomous tool calls from premium-request counts, consistent with this.)
answers.quote: Copilot activates a specialized research agent that gathers and processes information from your codebase, from relevant GitHub repositories, and from the web.

answers.question: Are there terms forbidding automated benchmarking of Copilot or publishing its outputs?
answers.answer: Not found. Checked three official governing-terms documents: GitHub Terms of Service (Section J, "AI Features, Training, and Your Data" — the section that explicitly governs Copilot for individual/non-enterprise users), GitHub Acceptable Use Policies, and the GitHub Generative AI Services Terms (which governs Business/Enterprise seats purchased direct from GitHub). None of the three contain the word "benchmark," and none contain an explicit clause forbidding automated benchmarking or publishing Copilot's outputs. A docs.github.com page titled "github-copilot-product-specific-terms" does not exist (404) — so there is no separate Copilot-specific acceptable-use document beyond these three. This is not proof no such restriction exists elsewhere (e.g., a signed enterprise/volume agreement could differ), only that it isn't in the three public documents checked.
answers.quote: This section applies to all AI Features unless a specific feature has additional terms that expressly modify them. The training and data-use provisions in Section J.3 apply only to individual licenses.

answers.question: Is there a $5 minimum first credit purchase for a new OpenAI API account, or pay-as-you-go with no minimum?
answers.answer: New API accounts are on prepaid billing, and the minimum initial credit purchase is $5 (default offered amount is $10). The 'no minimum, pay-as-you-go' claim applies only to legacy accounts still on old monthly invoiced billing, not to new accounts today (2026-09-18) — the two claims round 1 found aren't contradictory, they describe two different billing regimes, and new accounts get the $5-minimum prepaid one.
answers.quote: New API accounts use prepaid billing. ... Choose your initial credit purchase amount. The minimum purchase is $5, and the default amount is $10.

answers.question: For the Responses API web_search tool with gpt-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna and gpt-6-astra: is retrieved search content billed as input tokens at the model rate, or free?
answers.answer: Billed as input tokens at the model's standard rate, not free. The current 'web_search' tool (what these models use) is priced as '$10.00 / 1k calls + Search content tokens billed at model rates.' The 'content is free' pricing row exists only for the older, deprecated web_search_preview tool paired with non-reasoning models ($25/1k calls) — not applicable to gpt-5.6/gpt-6-astra. One narrow exception: gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini on the non-preview tool get a flat 8,000-input-token block per call instead of metered content billing — also not the models in question. Conflict flagged: openai.com/business/pricing shows the same $10/1k-call web search tier as 'Search content tokens are free,' with no per-model breakdown — that page contradicts the technical docs. Treat the developer pricing docs (this source) as authoritative for API billing; the business page reads like simplified marketing copy.
answers.quote: Web search (all models) ... $10.00 / 1k calls + Search content tokens billed at model rates.

answers.question: Does one answer typically make more than one search call, and is each billed?
answers.answer: Yes to both, per the official guide: reasoning models (the class gpt-5.6/gpt-6-astra belong to) use 'agentic search,' where the model can search repeatedly within one response and decide whether to keep searching; deep research explicitly 'often tap[s] into hundreds of sources.' Billing is defined per call ($10.00/1k calls), so every search call inside one response is metered and billed individually — no bundling or cap is stated. No official page gives a specific 'typical' number of calls per answer, so that exact figure is not stated anywhere I could find.
answers.quote: It can perform web searches as part of its chain of thought, analyze results, and decide whether to keep searching.

answers.question: Do prepaid credits expire, and when?
answers.answer: Yes. Purchased credits expire 1 year after purchase, and OpenAI will not extend that date for any credits or credit grants.
answers.quote: Purchased credits expire after 1 year. OpenAI cannot extend the expiration date of purchased credits or credit grants.

answers.question: Default reasoning effort for gpt-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna and gpt-6-astra and whether it can be set to none/minimal.
answers.answer: gpt-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna: default is medium; effort can be set to none (full list: none, low, medium(default), high, xhigh, max) — 'minimal' is NOT a listed option for any of the three. gpt-6-astra: supported values are only low, medium, high, xhigh, max — no 'none' and no 'minimal' option exists for this model, and its own model page does not state which of those is the default (answer: not stated).
answers.quote: Reasoning.effort supports: none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh, and max.

answers.question: Gemini 3.x Grounding with Google Search: is the $14/1,000 fee per search query or per grounded prompt, and does the 5,000 free searches/month apply only on the paid tier?
answers.answer: Per search query, not per grounded prompt. Google's own grounding doc says billing is per search query the model executes, and a single prompt that triggers multiple queries is billed for each one — this per-query model is specific to Gemini 3.x (Gemini 2.5 and older bill per prompt). The 5,000 free searches/month is paid-tier only: the pricing table's Free Tier column for Grounding with Google Search on every Gemini 3.x model (3.8 Flash, 3.1 Pro Preview, etc.) reads "Not available"; the 5,000-free-then-$14/1,000 allowance sits in the Paid Tier column.
answers.quote: When you use Grounding with Google Search with Gemini 3, your project is billed for each search query that the model decides to execute. ... This billing model only applies to Gemini 3 models; when you use search grounding with Gemini 2.5 or older models, your project is billed per prompt.

answers.question: Gemini 2.5 Flash / Flash-Lite: confirm free-tier grounding "up to 500 RPD" and paid "1,500 RPD free then $35 per 1,000 grounded prompts".
answers.answer: Confirmed exactly as stated for both Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite (RPD caps are shared between the two models).

answers.question: Is retrieved grounding content billed as input tokens for Gemini 3.x?
answers.answer: No. The pricing page explicitly calls out Search Grounding as the one tool where retrieved tokens are excluded from token billing (the flat per-query grounding fee covers it instead) — in contrast to URL context and File Search, where retrieved document/page tokens ARE billed as ordinary input tokens. This line is written as the general/standard billing distinction (it appears in the agents pricing section but is phrased as the pre-existing pricing structure, not an agent-only rule).
answers.quote: Tool usage fees apply per existing pricing structure, maintaining standard distinctions for Search Grounding (retrieved tokens excluded) versus Url_context / File Search (retrieved tokens included in all other tools).

answers.question: How is web search billed via the plugin/:online — engine, price per result or per request, default result count?
answers.answer: Important update first: OpenRouter's docs say the web plugin (plugins:[{id:"web"}]) and the :online suffix are now DEPRECATED in favor of a new openrouter:web_search server tool, though pricing/rates are stated to be identical between the two surfaces. Engine defaults to "auto": native provider search when the model supports it, else falls back to Exa. Billing is per REQUEST/call, not per result, bundling up to 10 results into that flat price (extra results beyond 10 cost $0.001 each, Exa/Parallel). Exa: $0.007/request (instant/fast/auto), $0.012 (deep-lite/deep), $0.015 (deep-reasoning). Parallel: $0.001/request (turbo/fast), $0.005/request (basic/advanced). Perplexity (as an engine choice): $0.005/request. Firecrawl: billed on your own Firecrawl credits, no OpenRouter charge. Default max_results parameter = 5 for non-native engines; ignored entirely for native search, which instead uses a search_context_size of low/medium/high (no explicit result count documented).
answers.quote: The web search plugin (plugins: [{ id: "web" }]) and the :online variant are deprecated. Use the openrouter:web_search server tool instead. ... Exa Instant/Fast/Auto: $0.007 per request; Deep Lite/Deep: $0.012; Deep Reasoning: $0.015. Includes up to 10 results, then $0.001 per additional result. ... max_results integer 5 Maximum results per search call (1–25; 1–20 for Perplexity). Applies to Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, and Perplexity engines; ignored with native provider search

answers.question: Does native search for OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/xAI bill the provider's own fee instead of an OpenRouter rate?
answers.answer: Yes, confirmed. Native search (used by default for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity, and xAI/"SpaceXAI" models when the model supports it) is priced as a straight pass-through of the provider's own native web-search fee, not a separate OpenRouter-set rate. On the model pages this shows up as a flat, provider-set "Web Search" figure: GPT-6 Astra $10.00/1K calls ($0.01/call), Gemini 3.8 Flash $14.00/1K calls ($0.014/call), Grok 4.6 $5.00/1K calls ($0.005/call), Sonar $5.00/1K calls ($0.005/call) — all matching Round 1's numbers exactly.
answers.quote: Native | Passed through from the provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity, SpaceXAI) ... All pricing is in addition to standard LLM token costs for processing the search result content.

answers.question: Does a paid balance raise the free-model daily limit (currently 50/day), and to what?
answers.answer: Yes. Once you have purchased at least $10 in credits (lifetime, all-time total, not current balance), the free-model daily request cap rises from 50/day to 1,000/day. The per-minute cap for free models is a flat 20 requests/minute regardless of purchase history. This exact set of numbers appears identically on two separate OpenRouter doc pages (FAQ and Limits), which is an independent double-confirmation.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS THAT LOOK WRONG OR STALE:
1. OpenRouter minimum purchase is wrong. Round 1 said it is not stated on any public page. The Terms of Service (sec 4.1, updated Aug 31, 2026) state a $5 minimum and $25,000 maximum per transaction. They also say unused credits are refundable only within 24 hours and platform fees never are.
2. OpenRouter "pass-through, no markup" is incomplete. The price depends on which provider endpoint serves the request. Sol is $2/$10 via OpenAI (a 50% discount flag with no stated end), $4.40/$22 via Bedrock and $5/$30 via Azure. Default load balancing can route some requests to the pricier endpoints.
3. The Perplexity preset finding uses Sol at $5/$30 as if that were the provider rate. OpenAI direct is currently $4/$20 (promo), so Perplexity is 25% higher on input and 50% higher on output. Perplexity refreshes prices only monthly.
4. The Perplexity "$0.007 low preset" worked example is stale, and it is on the Pricing page, not the Presets page. Its token lines imply $0.50/$3 per 1M tokens, but the low preset now runs gpt-5.6-luna at $0.20/$1.20. With Luna the same run costs about $0.0046: $0.0004 input + $0.0012 output + $0.0025 web_search + $0.0005 fetch_url.
5. The Gemini claim that grounding content is excluded from token billing was marked confirmed and general. The only source is the "Pricing for agents" rows. The grounding doc's own Pricing section and the per-model tables are silent. It should be downgraded to inferred.
6. The Copilot finding says the Gemini 3.6/3.7/3.8 rate after the promo is not stated. Copilot's page does not state it, but Google's own pricing page does: from Jan 1, 2027, input goes $0.75 to $1.50 and output $3.75 to $7.50. Whether Copilot follows Google is inferred.
7. The Copilot finding lists Sol and Astra credit rates without the plan gate. Copilot Pro ($10) excludes both; you need Pro+ ($39). That changes the Copilot cost by $29/month.
8. Copilot's web-search route is not comparable to the others. /research is documented for interactive sessions, its research agent defaults to claude-haiku-4.5 rather than the pinned model, and -p mode documents only web_fetch. The "with web search" arm would measure Haiku-assisted answers.
9. The Perplexity fast and low presets set Luna's reasoning effort to "minimal". OpenAI's Luna page lists only none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max. That is a doc inconsistency; I could not verify what Perplexity actually sends.
10. OpenAI's business pricing page says search content is free, which conflicts with the developer pricing page. Round 1 already flagged this; the developer pricing page (read this session) says content is billed at model rates.

TIME-SENSITIVE PRICE CHANGES:
- OpenAI Sol promo is guaranteed only through Nov 21, 2026.
- Gemini 3.x Flash prices double on Jan 1, 2027.
- Copilot's Gemini promo ends Dec 31, 2026.
- xAI X Search billing changes Sep 21, 2026. That is not web_search, but it is the same week.

LONG-CONTEXT STEPS:
The measured 159K max is under every step: OpenAI 272K, Copilot Luna 200K, Gemini 3.1 Pro 200K, xAI 200K, Perplexity 272K/200K. The margin is thinnest at 200K. xAI explicitly accumulates prompt tokens across agentic steps. Whether cumulative totals count toward the step threshold is not stated for any provider.

NOT STATED ANYWHERE I LOOKED:
- Perplexity: minimum purchase, credit expiry, sales tax.
- xAI: manual purchase minimum and credit expiry.
- OpenRouter: US sales tax specifically (the page names only VAT/GST).
- GPT-6 Astra: default reasoning effort.
- Azure: long-context threshold.
- Copilot: size of the CLI agent's system-prompt overhead per call.
